prompt: A bulk TCP transfer begins retransmitting more data after a cable fault. Assume the link remains fully busy with equal-sized transmission attempts. What does this establish about useful goodput?

options.text: It stays unchanged because every attempt contains payload
options.explanation: Failed or extra attempts consume capacity; useful delivered bytes are counted only once.

options.text: It decreases because extra attempts use wire time that could carry new payload
options.explanation: Correct under the stated saturated-link accounting. Real congestion responses can reduce it further.

options.text: It becomes equal to the raw line rate
options.explanation: Headers and retransmission work prevent that conclusion.

options.text: It must fall by exactly half for every loss event
options.explanation: No fixed factor follows from these facts; timers, windows and congestion control matter.

workedExample: Track a successfully delivered byte once, then count every transmission needed to deliver it. More extra attempts leave less of a fixed wire-time budget for new data. This is useful accounting, not a full TCP-performance model: loss may also cause backoff or timeouts.
